what_this_is: The Workshop row for the one Connections list: every service a person can connect (this folder's records.json) and every place on their own computer Trillion can read (tools/bring-in-new-items-from-this-computer computer/computer-sources.json), in one list read from the two owners' rows.

payload.label: List everything I can connect, services and my computer's places together
payload.job: Show every service I can connect to Trillion and every place on my own computer it can read (notes, voice memos, messages, photos, downloads), in one list grouped by kind
payload.description: One list of every connection a person can make: each service (how it connects: a key, a sign-in, or carried by their computer, with the steps for one carried) and each place on their own computer (what it arrives as, and the switch it needs). Optionally give category (one group, such as Messages or Pictures) and looked, the answer of tool:look-for-the-places-on-this-computer, so each place says whether it is on the computer (found, needs_switch, could_not_check, not_here); without it a place is not_looked. Reads rows only: it connects, looks at and sends nothing, and shows no secret. Returns said and connections ({ id, kind: service | computer-place, label, category, how, ... }), sorted by category then label.

category.description: Only this group, such as Messages, Pictures or Calendar

payload.label: Trade a Gmail sign-in code for its tokens
payload.job: Trade the code Google's sign-in page handed back for the connection's access and refresh tokens, kept sealed in the vault
payload.description: One token request to Google (the google-account descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form, PKCE): the code, the callback address and the PKCE verifier go in a form body with the Google sign-in app's id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token, refresh_token and id_token are kept in the vault as the new connection's own fields (reply_holds_values) before the reply is read, so no token is ever in a run's answer or journal; a field already held is never replaced and then nothing is sent. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

connection_id.description: The new connection the sign-in fills: service_connection:<vendor>:<account>, made by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service when the sign-in started

connection.description: The connection whose held fields the reply fills, by its handle only

code.description: The code the service handed back to the sign-in callback

redirect_uri.description: The callback address the sign-in was started with

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier the sign-in was started with (RFC 7636)

output_schema.description: The service's token reply, each kept token replaced by the held word

payload.label: Trade an Instagram sign-in code for its short-lived token
payload.job: Trade the code Instagram's sign-in page handed back for the connection's short-lived token, kept sealed in the vault
payload.description: One token request to Instagram (the instagram descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form): the code and the callback address go in a form body with the Instagram login's app id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token (Instagram's short-lived token) is kept in the vault as the new connection's field short_lived_access_token before the reply is read; tool:trade-a-short-instagram-token-for-a-long-one then trades it for the 60-day token (the descriptor's acquire.then). Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

payload.label: Trade a short-lived Instagram token for a long-lived one
payload.job: Trade the connection's short-lived Instagram token for its 60-day token, kept sealed in the vault
payload.description: The instagram descriptor's acquire.then step: GET graph.instagram.com/access_token with grant_type ig_exchange_token, the Instagram login's app secret and the connection's short-lived token, both placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token is kept in the vault as the connection's access_token field before the reply is read. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback, right after tool:trade-an-instagram-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token.
